text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Compared to New York robusta futures in London remained fairly stable. Traders said supplies of robustas are ample due to coffees which did not re-grade under the exchange's new criteria, in effect from the July delivery period. In spite of low seasonal demand from roasters, market sources said there was still limited trade buying under current prices to support the nearby contract. September closed $5 lower at $1,655 per tonne, while November remained unchanged at $1,655 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York saw a downward correction as speculators took profits following two straight sessions of hefty gains. Roasters said they have sufficient supplies but the question is whether the supplies will last long enough until the new harvest comes in. Despite today's losses the downturn is probably more a temporary setback as concerns about a shortage of exchange-certified coffees for delivery against the September contract persist and are reflected in the steady buying of the nearby September/December switch. The September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, widened to 30.30 cents/lb compared with 28.40 cents/lb on Tuesday. September lost 2.55 cents/lb to close at 200.55 cents/lb. December closed 4.45 cents/lb easier at 170.25 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - The Brazilian government sold 99.37 per cent or 85,570 60-kg bags of the 85,800 bags of coffee stocks offered to all segments of the coffee sector in its auction on August 6, according to the Banco do Brasil. Total revenue for the government was 13.54 million reais ($12.42 million).

Closing prices for arabica coffee were up to 30 reais higher than opening levels set by the government. The one lot of robusta coffee was sold for 130.05 reais a bag, up 49.05 reais from the opening price of 81 reais.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 938 bags as of August 5 to 92,459 bags. An additional 6,447 bags were pending grading.

ITALY ** - Italy imported 521,901 bags of coffee in March 1997, 1.3 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 1.518 million bags, 1.6 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 4 per cent to 5.608 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Ivory Coast (100,300 vs 76,200 bags), Uganda (132,200 vs 96,800 bags), Zaire (110,600 vs 148,100 bags) and Brazil (403,400 vs 365,500 bags).

The country exported 216,100 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, nearly 12 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 11 per cent to 822,500 bags.
